1	"""Single-file SQL query layer.
2	
3	Public API:
4	
5	* :func:`query_file` -- run a ``SELECT ... FROM input [WHERE ...]`` query
6	  against one columnar file and return a :class:`~columnar_analytics.format.Table`
7	* :func:`query_files` -- run a statement (optionally with one equi-join)
8	  against a table-name to path mapping
9	* :func:`explain_file` / :func:`explain_files` -- parse, bind and plan the
10	  same statements without executing them; only file metadata is read
11	* :class:`QuerySyntaxError` -- lexical / grammatical errors
12	* :class:`QueryValidationError` -- unknown columns, wrong table name,
13	  type-incompatible comparisons, invalid aggregate use
14	
15	The accepted grammar (keywords case-insensitive)::
16	
17	    query       := SELECT [DISTINCT] select_item (',' select_item)*
18	                   FROM ident [WHERE expr] [GROUP BY ident (',' ident)*]
19	                   [HAVING expr]
20	                   [ORDER BY order_item (',' order_item)*]
21	                   [LIMIT uint]
22	    select_item := '*' | ident | agg_name '(' ('*' | ident) ')'
23	                   | scalar_expr AS alias
24	    order_item  := (ident | agg_name '(' ('*' | ident) ')')
25	                   [ASC | DESC] [NULLS FIRST | NULLS LAST]
26	    expr       := or_expr
27	    or_expr     := and_expr (OR and_expr)*
28	    and_expr    := cmp_expr (AND cmp_expr)*
29	    cmp_expr    := not_factor (cmp_op not_factor)?
30	    not_factor  := NOT not_factor | postfix
31	    postfix     := scalar_expr (IS [NOT] NULL)?
32	    scalar_expr := term (('+' | '-') term)*
33	    term        := factor (('*' | '/') factor)*
34	    factor      := ('+' | '-') factor | atom
35	    atom        := '(' expr ')' | operand
36	                | CASE WHEN expr THEN scalar_expr
37	                  (WHEN expr THEN scalar_expr)*
38	                  (ELSE scalar_expr)? END
39	    operand     := ident | literal
40	    literal     := TRUE | FALSE | [+-]? int64 | [+-]? finite float64
41	                   | single-quoted utf8
42	
43	The supported aggregates are ``COUNT(*)``, ``COUNT(ident)`` and
44	``SUM`` / ``AVG`` / ``MIN`` / ``MAX`` applied to one column.  Without
45	GROUP BY the projection may contain aggregate expressions only; with
46	GROUP BY it may additionally contain the grouped columns.  A bare ``*``
47	must not be mixed with aggregates or grouping.  Aggregates are not
48	allowed inside WHERE, may not be nested, and aliases are not supported
49	for bare columns or aggregate calls.
50	
51	Scalar arithmetic (parentheses, unary ``+``/``-``, binary ``+`` ``-``
52	``*`` ``/``; precedence: parentheses, unary, ``*``/``/``, ``+``/``-``)
53	is available over int64 / float64 columns and numeric literals in SELECT
54	and WHERE.  A computed SELECT expression must be named with ``AS`` (the
55	alias follows the usual identifier rules and must be unique among the
56	output names); bare columns and aggregate calls keep their existing
57	result names.  int64 ``+``/``-``/``*`` on two int64 operands yields
58	int64; any float64 operand or a division yields float64, and unary
59	operators preserve the operand type.  Any NULL operand makes the result
60	NULL; the output column is nullable iff a participating column is
61	nullable (pure constants are not).  int64 overflow, division by zero and
62	non-finite float64 results raise :class:`QueryValidationError`.  A
63	numeric expression used directly as a boolean condition is rejected with
64	:class:`QueryValidationError` as well.  Non-aggregate queries execute
65	WHERE, then compute the sort keys, stably sort, apply LIMIT and only
66	then evaluate the SELECT expressions, so filtered or truncated rows
67	never trigger division-by-zero or overflow in the projection; a
68	DISTINCT query instead evaluates the projection right after WHERE,
69	deduplicates the result rows, and only then sorts and applies LIMIT.  ORDER BY
70	may name a SELECT alias (an alias shadows an input column of the same
71	name) and sorts on the expression's result type with the usual NULL
72	placement and stability rules.  Aggregate queries do not accept scalar
73	expressions: GROUP BY keys and aggregate arguments stay plain column
74	references, and mixing a scalar expression into an aggregate query
75	raises :class:`QueryValidationError`.
76	
77	``SELECT DISTINCT`` removes duplicate rows from a non-aggregate query:
78	the projection may be a star, plain columns or ``AS``-aliased scalar
79	expressions exactly as without DISTINCT, and deduplication compares the
80	full projected result row column by column after WHERE.  Two NULLs in
81	the same result column compare equal, NULL never equals a non-NULL
82	value, bool / utf8 / numeric values keep their existing comparison
83	semantics, and float64 ``0.0`` and ``-0.0`` compare equal.  Without
84	ORDER BY the surviving rows keep the order of the first occurrence of
85	each distinct result row; ORDER BY then sorts the deduplicated rows and
86	LIMIT keeps the first N.  The projection expressions are evaluated
87	only for rows that passed WHERE (and, with ORDER BY, before the sort),
88	so a division by zero, int64 overflow or non-finite float64 result that
89	actually occurs still raises :class:`QueryValidationError`.  ORDER BY
90	of a DISTINCT query may name only bare columns or explicit aliases that
91	are part of the projection; an unprojected or otherwise unknown name
92	raises :class:`QueryValidationError`, and the sort direction, NULL
93	placement and stability rules are unchanged.  DISTINCT combined with
94	GROUP BY, HAVING or any aggregate projection raises
95	:class:`QueryValidationError`; ``COUNT(DISTINCT ...)`` is not part of
96	the grammar.  A missing projection, a repeated DISTINCT or a misplaced
97	DISTINCT keyword raises :class:`QuerySyntaxError` before any file is
98	opened.
99	
100	Searched CASE expressions
101	(``CASE WHEN cond THEN result [WHEN ...] [ELSE result] END``; the simple
102	``CASE value WHEN ...`` form is not supported and at least one WHEN is
103	required) are scalar operands and may be nested inside more arithmetic,
104	comparisons and other CASE expressions.  For each row the WHEN conditions
105	are tested in written order and only TRUE matches; FALSE and UNKNOWN fall
106	through, an explicit ELSE supplies the fallback and a missing ELSE yields
107	NULL.  Only the chosen result is evaluated, so division by zero, int64
108	overflow or a non-finite float64 inside an unhit branch never raises; a
109	chosen result that errors still raises :class:`QueryValidationError`.
110	Every reachable THEN and an explicit ELSE must share one type family:
111	int64 and float64 may mix and unify to float64, while bool and utf8 must
112	match each other exactly (any other mix raises
113	:class:`QueryValidationError`).  The result column is nullable if any
114	reachable result is nullable or the ELSE is omitted.  WHEN conditions use
115	the same boolean type check and three-valued logic as WHERE; CASE stays a
116	scalar expression, so it is rejected in aggregate arguments, GROUP BY and
117	the projection of an aggregate query just like the other scalar
118	expressions.
119	
120	Operator precedence (highest first) is NOT, comparison, AND, OR; IS [NOT]
121	NULL is a postfix of its scalar operand.  Comparison operands may be
122	column references, literals or scalar arithmetic expressions.  WHERE
123	follows SQL three-valued logic: a normal
124	comparison against NULL yields UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN propagates through the
125	logical operators, and only TRUE rows are returned.
126	
127	After WHERE, rows are grouped in GROUP BY column order (a NULL key forms
128	its own group); without an explicit ORDER BY groups come out in the order
129	of their first selected row.  An optional HAVING clause between GROUP BY
130	and ORDER BY filters the formed groups with the same boolean expression
131	grammar and three-valued logic as WHERE: its conditions combine grouping
132	columns, aggregate calls and type-compatible literals with NOT / AND / OR
133	/ comparisons / IS [NOT] NULL, only groups whose condition is TRUE are
134	kept, and aggregates named in HAVING need not appear in SELECT.  Without
135	GROUP BY HAVING filters the single global aggregate row (still produced
136	when WHERE selected no rows); with GROUP BY an empty selection yields
137	zero groups.  HAVING may not name ungrouped plain columns, ``*``, CASE,
138	scalar arithmetic or nested aggregates; it is rejected on a completely
139	non-aggregate query.  ORDER BY may only name a selected result; ASC is the
140	default, NULLs sort last regardless of direction unless NULLS FIRST /
141	NULLS LAST is given, and groups equal on every sort key keep that
142	first-row order.  LIMIT then keeps the first N groups.  Without GROUP BY
143	and aggregates an aggregate query over zero selected rows still yields one
144	output row (COUNT 0, the other aggregates NULL), unless HAVING removes it;
145	with GROUP BY it yields zero rows.
146	
147	Two-file queries (:func:`query_files`) add one equi-join to the grammar::
148	
149	    query := SELECT ... FROM left_table [join_kind JOIN right_table
150	             ON left_table.column = right_table.column] ...
151	    join_kind := INNER | LEFT | RIGHT | FULL OUTER
152	
153	``sources`` maps table names to file paths; only the tables referenced by
154	the statement are read.  Aliases, compound ON conditions, other join
155	types, ``FULL`` without ``OUTER`` and a second join are rejected as syntax
156	errors before any file is opened.  In a join query every column reference
157	outside ``COUNT(*)`` must be qualified as ``table.column`` (either part may
158	be a double-quoted identifier).  ``SELECT *`` emits the left schema
159	followed by the right schema with ``table.column`` names; explicit
160	projections keep their qualified names and aggregates keep the uppercase
161	``FUNC(table.column)`` labels.  Join keys may share a type or mix int64
162	with float64; NULL keys never match.  INNER JOIN emits every matching
163	combination, LEFT JOIN also emits unmatched left rows with the right-side
164	values set to NULL (the right result columns are nullable), RIGHT JOIN
165	emits all right rows in right-file order (one right row's matches expand
166	in left-file order) padding the left side with NULL (the left result
167	columns are nullable), and FULL OUTER JOIN emits the LEFT JOIN output and
168	then appends the unmatched right rows in right-file order (both sides are
169	nullable).  Matched combinations always expand in left-file order (within
170	one left row in right-file order) before WHERE / GROUP BY / HAVING /
171	ORDER BY / LIMIT apply with their usual semantics.
172	
173	The multi-file entry points (:func:`query_files`, :func:`explain_files`)
174	take an optional ``join_strategy`` of ``"hash"`` or ``"sort_merge"``.
175	Both strategies accept the same statements and return identical column
176	descriptions, values, NULL placement and row order; they differ only in
177	how matching right rows are located (a right-key hash index versus
178	sorting both sides on the key and merging equal-key runs).  With the
179	argument omitted the historical join path is used and the explain plan
180	is unchanged; with an explicit strategy the plan's Join operator gains a
181	``strategy`` field of ``HASH`` or ``SORT_MERGE``.  A JOIN-less statement
182	accepts either strategy but gains no extra operator, and an invalid
183	strategy raises :class:`ValueError` before any source file is opened.
184	"""
185	
186	from __future__ import annotations
187	
188	import math
189	import os
190	import re

200	    "QueryValidationError",
201	    "explain_file",
202	    "explain_files",
203	    "query_file",
204	    "query_files",
205	]
206	
207	_KEYWORDS = frozenset(
208	    (
209	        "select",
210	        "distinct",
211	        "from",
212	        "where",
213	        "as",
214	        "not",
215	        "and",
216	        "or",
217	        "is",
218	        "null",

220	        "false",
221	        "order",

243	# Aggregate function names are ordinary (case-insensitive) identifiers that
244	# gain call syntax only in the projection and ORDER BY.
245	_AGG_NAMES = frozenset(("count", "sum", "avg", "min", "max"))
246	_INT64_MIN = -(2**63)
247	_INT64_MAX = 2**63 - 1
248	
249	# Optional join strategies for two-file queries.  ``None`` keeps the implicit
250	# historical path (a right-key hash lookup).  ``HASH`` is that same path
251	# requested explicitly; ``SORT_MERGE`` sorts both sides on the join key and
252	# merges the runs.  Both produce byte-identical results; only the explicit
253	# spellings surface in the explain plan.
254	_JOIN_STRATEGIES = frozenset(("hash", "sort_merge"))
255	_JOIN_STRATEGY_LABELS = {"hash": "HASH", "sort_merge": "SORT_MERGE"}

257	
258	def _validate_join_strategy(join_strategy: Any) -> str | None:
259	    """Validate the optional ``join_strategy`` argument.
260	
261	    Returns the canonical lowercase strategy name, or ``None`` when the
262	    caller did not request one.  Any other value (including a non-string)
263	    raises :class:`ValueError`; callers run this before opening any file.
264	    """
265	    if join_strategy is None:
266	        return None
267	    if not isinstance(join_strategy, str) or join_strategy not in _JOIN_STRATEGIES:
268	        allowed = ", ".join(sorted(_JOIN_STRATEGIES))
269	        raise ValueError(
270	            f"invalid join_strategy: {join_strategy!r}; expected one of {allowed}"
271	        )
272	    return join_strategy

274	
275	class QuerySyntaxError(Exception):
276	    """Raised when a query is lexically or grammatically invalid."""
277	
278	
279	class QueryValidationError(Exception):
280	    """Raised when a syntactically valid query is incompatible with the schema."""
281	
282	
283	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
284	# Tokeniser
285	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
286	
287	
288	@dataclass(frozen=True)
289	class _Token:
290	    kind: str  # one of: keyword, ident, number, string, op, star, eof
291	    value: Any
292	    text: str
293	
294	
295	_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(
296	    r"""
297	    \d+(?:\.\d*)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?   # 1, 1., 1.5, 1e3, 1.5e-2
298	    | \.\d+(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?         # .5
299	    """,
300	    re.VERBOSE,
301	)
302	# Bare identifiers: Unicode letters/underscore first, then word characters.
303	_IDENT_RE = re.compile(r"[^\W\d]\w*", re.UNICODE)
304	
305	
306	def _tokenize(sql: str) -> list[_Token]:
307	    if not isinstance(sql, str):
308	        raise QuerySyntaxError("SQL statement must be a string")
309	    tokens: list[_Token] = []
310	    i = 0
311	    n = len(sql)
312	    while i < n:
313	        ch = sql[i]
314	        if ch.isspace():
315	            i += 1
316	            continue
317	        if ch == "*":
318	            tokens.append(_Token("star", None, ch))
319	            i += 1
320	            continue
321	        if ch in ",()+-/":
322	            tokens.append(_Token("op", ch, ch))
323	            i += 1
324	            continue
325	        if ch in "=<>!":
326	            if ch == "!" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "=":
327	                tokens.append(_Token("op", "!=", "!="))
328	                i += 2
329	                continue
330	            if ch in "<>" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "=":
331	                op = ch + "="
332	                tokens.append(_Token("op", op, op))
333	                i += 2
334	                continue
335	            if ch in "=<>":
336	                tokens.append(_Token("op", ch, ch))
337	                i += 1
338	                continue
339	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected character '!' at position {i}")
340	        if ch == "'":
341	            value, new_i = _tokenize_string(sql, i)
342	            tokens.append(_Token("string", value, sql[i:new_i]))
343	            i = new_i
344	            continue
345	        if ch == '"':
346	            value, new_i = _tokenize_quoted_ident(sql, i)
347	            tokens.append(_token_from_word(value, quoted=True))
348	            i = new_i
349	            continue
350	        if ch.isdigit() or ch == ".":
351	            match = _NUMBER_RE.match(sql, i)
352	            if match:
353	                text = match.group(0)
354	                tokens.append(_Token("number", _parse_number(text), text))
355	                i = match.end()
356	                continue
357	            # A '.' that does not start a number is the qualifier separator
358	            # used by two-table queries ("table.column").
359	            tokens.append(_Token("op", ".", ch))
360	            i += 1
361	            continue
362	        match = _IDENT_RE.match(sql, i)
363	        if match:
364	            text = match.group(0)
365	            tokens.append(_token_from_word(text, quoted=False))
366	            i = match.end()
367	            continue
368	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected character {ch!r} at position {i}")
369	    tokens.append(_Token("eof", None, ""))
370	    return tokens
371	
372	
373	def _token_from_word(word: str, *, quoted: bool) -> _Token:
374	    lowered = word.lower()
375	    if not quoted and lowered in _KEYWORDS:
376	        if lowered == "true":
377	            return _Token("number", True, word)
378	        if lowered == "false":
379	            return _Token("number", False, word)
380	        return _Token("keyword", lowered, word)
381	    return _Token("qident" if quoted else "ident", word, word)
382	
383	
384	def _tokenize_string(sql: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
385	    parts: list[str] = []
386	    i = start + 1
387	    n = len(sql)
388	    while True:
389	        j = sql.find("'", i)
390	        if j == -1:
391	            raise QuerySyntaxError("unterminated string literal")
392	        parts.append(sql[i:j])
393	        if j + 1 < n and sql[j + 1] == "'":
394	            parts.append("'")
395	            i = j + 2
396	            continue
397	        value = "".join(parts)
398	        try:
399	            value.encode("utf-8")
400	        except UnicodeEncodeError:
401	            raise QuerySyntaxError("string literal is not valid UTF-8") from None
402	        return value, j + 1
403	
404	
405	def _tokenize_quoted_ident(sql: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
406	    parts: list[str] = []
407	    i = start + 1
408	    n = len(sql)
409	    while True:
410	        j = sql.find('"', i)
411	        if j == -1:
412	            raise QuerySyntaxError("unterminated quoted identifier")
413	        parts.append(sql[i:j])
414	        if j + 1 < n and sql[j + 1] == '"':
415	            parts.append('"')
416	            i = j + 2
417	            continue
418	        value = "".join(parts)
419	        if not value:
420	            raise QuerySyntaxError("quoted identifier must not be empty")
421	        return value, j + 1
422	
423	
424	def _parse_number(text: str) -> int | float:
425	    try:
426	        if any(ch in text for ch in ".eE"):
427	            value: int | float = float(text)
428	        else:
429	            value = int(text, 10)
430	    except ValueError:
431	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"invalid numeric literal {text!r}") from None
432	    if isinstance(value, int):
433	        # The magnitude 2**63 is accepted unsigned; the signed range check
434	        # happens after the optional leading sign is applied.
435	        if not (0 <= value <= 2**63):
436	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"integer literal {text} is outside the int64 range")
437	        return value
438	    if not math.isfinite(value):
439	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"float literal {text} must be finite")
440	    return value
441

443	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
444	# Parsed expression tree
445	#
446	# Node tuples:
447	#   ("literal", python_value, type_name)
448	#   ("column", name, table|None, table_quoted)        -- as parsed
449	#   ("column", name, index, type_name, nullable)      -- after binding
450	#   ("arith", op, left_node, right_node)              -- as parsed (+ - * /)
451	#   ("arith", op, left_node, right_node, type_name)   -- after binding
452	#   ("unary", operand, negate)                        -- as parsed
453	#   ("unary", operand, negate, type_name)             -- after binding
454	#   ("case", ((cond, result), ...), else_node|None)   -- as parsed
455	#   ("case", ((cond, result), ...), else_node|None, type_name) -- after binding
456	#   ("cmp", op, left_node, right_node)
457	#   ("isnull", operand, negate)
458	#   ("not", operand)

461	# "literal"/"column"/"arith"/"unary" nodes are value nodes.
462	#
463	# Projection / ORDER BY reference items:

465	#   ("agg", func_upper, arg_name|None)   -- an aggregate call; arg None = '*'
466	#   ("expr", alias)                      -- a computed scalar expression

491

531	    def __init__(self, tokens: list[_Token], allow_join: bool = False):
532	        self.tokens = tokens
533	        self.pos = 0
534	        # Two-table statements (qualified names + one JOIN clause) are only
535	        # enabled for query_files; single-file entry points keep rejecting
536	        # them as syntax errors.
537	        self._allow_join = allow_join

539	    def parse(self) -> _Select:
540	        select = self._parse_select()
541	        if self._peek().kind != "eof":
542	            tok = self._peek()
543	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected trailing input {tok.text!r}")
544	        return select

546	    def _parse_select(self) -> _Select:
547	        self._expect_keyword("select")
548	        distinct = self._accept_keyword("distinct")
549	        items = tuple(self._parse_projection())
550	        self._expect_keyword("from")
551	        table_tok = self._expect_table_name()
552	        join = None
553	        if self._allow_join:
554	            if self._accept_keyword("inner"):
555	                self._expect_keyword("join")
556	                join = self._parse_join("inner")
557	            elif self._accept_keyword("left"):
558	                self._expect_keyword("join")
559	                join = self._parse_join("left")
560	            elif self._accept_word("right"):
561	                self._expect_keyword("join")
562	                join = self._parse_join("right")
563	            elif self._accept_word("full"):
564	                # Only the explicit FULL OUTER JOIN spelling is accepted;
565	                # "right" / "full" / "outer" stay ordinary identifiers away
566	                # from this clause so single-file behaviour is unchanged.
567	                self._expect_word("outer")
568	                self._expect_keyword("join")
569	                join = self._parse_join("full")
570	        where = None
571	        if self._accept_keyword("where"):
572	            where = self._parse_or()
573	        group_by = None
574	        if self._accept_keyword("group"):
575	            self._expect_keyword("by")
576	            names = [self._parse_group_name()]
577	            while self._accept_op(","):
578	                names.append(self._parse_group_name())
579	            group_by = tuple(names)
580	        having = None
581	        if self._accept_keyword("having"):
582	            having = self._parse_having_or()
583	        order_by = None

587	            while self._accept_op(","):
588	                order_items.append(self._parse_order_item())
589	            order_by = tuple(order_items)

591	        if self._accept_keyword("limit"):
592	            limit = self._parse_limit()

594	            items=items,
595	            table=table_tok.value,
596	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
597	            where=where,
598	            group_by=group_by,
599	            having=having,
600	            order_by=order_by,
601	            limit=limit,
602	            join=join,

613	            kind=kind,

620	    def _parse_on_key(self) -> tuple:
621	        tok = self._peek()
622	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
623	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
624	                f"ON requires table-qualified columns, got {tok.text!r}"
625	            )
626	        self._next()
627	        if not self._accept_op("."):
628	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
629	                "ON requires table-qualified columns (table.column)"
630	            )

639	    def _parse_projection(self) -> list[_RefItem]:
640	        items = [self._parse_select_item()]
641	        while self._accept_op(","):
642	            items.append(self._parse_select_item())
643	        # Aliases are only supported for computed scalar expressions (which
644	        # consume their own "AS alias" in _parse_select_item); a trailing
645	        # identifier (including the spelling "as") where FROM is expected
646	        # names one on a bare column or aggregate.  Plain queries keep their
647	        # historical QuerySyntaxError classification; aggregate queries treat
648	        # the unsupported alias as a validation error.
649	        tok = self._peek()
650	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident") or (
651	            tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "as"
652	        ):
653	            grouped_ahead = any(
654	                t.kind == "keyword" and t.value == "group"
655	                for t in self.tokens[self.pos :]
656	            )
657	            if any(item.kind == "agg" for item in items) or grouped_ahead:
658	                raise QueryValidationError(
659	                    f"aliases are not supported; unexpected {tok.text!r} after projection item"
660	                )
661	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected FROM, got {tok.text!r}")
662	        return items

664	    def _parse_select_item(self) -> _RefItem:
665	        tok = self._peek()
666	        if tok.kind == "star":
667	            self._next()
668	            return _RefItem("star")
669	        if (
670	            tok.kind == "ident"
671	            and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES
672	            and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].kind == "op"
673	            and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].value == "("
674	        ):
675	            item = self._parse_column_or_agg()
676	            if self._arith_op_ahead():
677	                raise QueryValidationError(
678	                    "aggregate calls cannot be combined with scalar arithmetic"
679	                )
680	            return item
681	        node = self._parse_arith()
682	        if node[0] == "column":
683	            # A bare (possibly parenthesised) column reference keeps its
684	            # existing projection behaviour and needs no alias.
685	            return _RefItem(
686	                "column", name=node[1], table=node[2], table_quoted=node[3]
687	            )
688	        # A computed scalar expression must be named with AS.
689	        self._expect_keyword("as")
690	        alias = self._peek()
691	        if alias.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
692	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
693	                f"AS requires a result name, got {alias.text!r}"
694	            )
695	        self._next()
696	        return _RefItem("expr", name=alias.value, expr=node)

698	    def _arith_op_ahead(self) -> bool:

739	    def _parse_qualified_column(self) -> _RefItem:
740	        # Current token starts "table.column"; consumes all three tokens.

747	            )

750	            "column",
751	            name=name_tok.value,
752	            table=table_tok.value,

754	        )

756	    def _parse_column_or_agg(self) -> _RefItem:
757	        tok = self._peek()
758	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
759	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected identifier, got {tok.text!r}")
760	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
761	            return self._parse_qualified_column()

765	            self._next()

771	            # already consumed, so it is a plain column reference.
772	            return _RefItem("column", name=tok.value)

774	        self._expect_op(")")
775	        return _RefItem(
776	            "agg",
777	            func=func.upper(),
778	            arg=arg,
779	            arg_table=arg_table,
780	            arg_table_quoted=arg_table_quoted,
781	        )

783	    def _parse_aggregate_args(self, func: str) -> tuple:
784	        # Exactly one argument: '*' for COUNT, otherwise one (possibly
785	        # table-qualified) identifier.  Returns (name, table, table_quoted);
786	        # name "" stands for '*'.

789	            raise QueryValidationError(
790	                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column reference, not a CASE expression"
791	            )
792	        if tok.kind == "star":
793	            if func != "count":
794	                raise QuerySyntaxError(f"{func.upper()} does not accept '*'")

796	            return ("", None, False)
797	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
798	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
799	                f"{func.upper()} requires one column argument, got {tok.text!r}"
800	            )
801	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
802	            item = self._parse_qualified_column()
803	            nxt = self._peek()
804	            if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
805	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
806	                    f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column name, not a function call"
807	                )
808	            self._reject_expression_in_agg_arg(func)
809	            return (item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted)
810	        self._next()
811	        nxt = self._peek()
812	        if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
813	            if tok.kind == "ident" and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES:
814	                raise QueryValidationError(
815	                    f"aggregate functions must not be nested: "
816	                    f"{func.upper()}({tok.value.upper()}(...))"
817	                )
818	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
819	                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column name, not a function call"
820	            )

822	        return (tok.value, None, False)

859	            )

864	            result = (item.table, item.table_quoted, item.name)

870	        if self._arith_op_ahead():

877	    #
878	    # HAVING shares the WHERE boolean structure (NOT / AND / OR / comparison /

881	    # scalar arithmetic and nested aggregates are rejected.

883	    def _parse_having_or(self) -> tuple:

895	    def _parse_having_comparison(self) -> tuple:

897	        tok = self._peek()
